catalogue_requests.reason: No catalogue class covers starting, arming, stopping or factory-resetting a trigger sequence. cap.device.configure.v1 is a state-write class, and the card's cap.sensing.read.v1 binds only sensor resource kinds; neither expresses the arm/run/arm_and_run/stop/factory_reset lifecycle of the PQSC.
No catalogue class covers blocking until a trigger sequence and its feedback processing are done. The wait is an action with an operator-bounded timeout, not a sensor read or a state write.

notes:
DEVIATION FROM THE CARD: the QcodesDriver helper cannot bind this device. ZIBaseInstrument.__init__ creates the QCoDeS Parameters with init_nodetree from the connected device's LabOne node tree (src/zhinst/qcodes/driver/devices/base.py:46, src/zhinst/qcodes/qcodes_adaptions.py:772), not as explicit self.<name> = Parameter(...) assignments, which is the only form the QcodesDriver source proof accepts. This package is therefore a direct Driver over the card's ast-confirmed entry class zhinst.qcodes.driver.devices.pqsc:PQSC. SERVED: the upstream identity and streaming-node reads (get_idn, get_streamingnodes), the reference-clock check (check_ref_clock), and the trigger lifecycle arm/run/arm_and_run/stop/factory_reset plus wait_done as two x-cap extension actions. NOT COVERED: the dynamically generated LabOne node Parameters and their per-node units and ranges (their names come from the node tree, not from a citable source line); set_transaction (a context manager for bundling node sets, not a value or an action); the optional repetitions and holdoff arguments of arm/arm_and_run (no source states their bounds; the hold-off docstring gives only a minimum value and a granularity of 100 ns, so the package calls the methods without them, which the upstream documents as not changing them); check_zsync_connection and find_zsync_worker_port (they need a concrete ZSync port list or a toolkit instrument object this device-level package does not own). The fake is an analytic F0 stand-in, not a recording: it keeps canned private state (each value marked # placeholder), does not open a LabOne session, does not read the node tree, does not model ZSync ports, trigger counts, hold-off timing or feedback processing, and wait_done returns immediately. The real streaming-node list and all identity values come from the connected device. HARDWARE: native.py exposes connect() and builds the upstream subclass zhinst.qcodes.device_creator:PQSC (an instance of the selected pqsc:PQSC class) after the operator supplies the serial and the LabOne data-server host and port; it needs the upstream zhinst-qcodes/zhinst-toolkit/qcodes and LabOne client dependencies. It was never run and no hardware was attached; the package has never opened a LabOne session. The native stop is PQSC.stop(deep=False): it disables trigger generation and does not wait for a deep synchronization, but it does not stop the connected instruments' own acquisition loops and does not clear settings. site-limits.example.json is an example operator overlay that fills the operator-required wait_done timeout; without it every wait_done invocation carrying a timeout is refused MHS.SAFETY.LIMITS_UNSET. The upstream clone at 042dd17a5bf492cc4c573e465b2bc399e68d3203 was read only and remained unmodified. Evidence is contract_checked on the fake backend only, never a hardware run.

MODEL REVIEW (claude-opus-5-5, a model and not a human, 2026-11-05; reviewed_by stays null): Checked the direct-Driver deviation against the readiness evidence (blocked: QcodesDriver cannot prove the node tree init_nodetree generates, base.py:46; a direct Driver over the PQSC class's explicit methods, pqsc.py:10-181, is a provable subset the evidence did not consider and serves its primary control, the trigger lifecycle), R1, the operator-required wait timeout, every fact, native.py and the stop. Defects: the e-stop called stop(deep=False), which per the clone's docstring returns before the device/data-server synchronization (pqsc.py:52-61), so a completed e-stop proved only that the request was handed to the session; the firmware read declared a string while get_idn() returns the system/fwrevision node value (base.py:48-55), whose type the clone does not show (its test node doc types /zi/about/fwrevision as Integer (64 bit)), and the streaming_nodes read assumed string entries; the fake's string placeholders hid both. The reviewer made the e-stop call stop(deep=True) (a slow sync is reported SAFE_STATE_UNREACHED by the runtime budget and retried), made both reads return text, rewrote safe_state and the docstring, widened the stop fact and added two (a deep node operation blocks until the device acknowledged it, qcodes_adaptions.py:279-282; the unpinned zhinst-toolkit dependency, pyproject.toml:22-27) (driver.py); made the firmware placeholder an integer (fake.py); asserted the deep stop and added two cases (a raising stop leaves the e-stop unreached with the latch held; non-string identity and node values read as text) (test_driver.py); updated facts.md and regenerated reference.json, REFERENCE.md and check-report.json. The gate passes with the digest unchanged (sha256:49bb4b23589d3e09d64b21769330d2f540c5eb2126b83fa9c387b2c23669877f); the author's note on stop(deep=False) is superseded. For the human reviewer: PQSC trigger distributor at R1: run and arm_and_run start triggers to every ZSync-connected instrument, which then play their own programs; factory_reset, served in the same action, loads factory defaults. The stop and every served method forward to zhinst-toolkit (not in the clone, >=1.4.0, unpinned), so the stop's effect is documented, not code-proven, and it neither stops nor resets the connected instruments. Whether the LabOne session tolerates the e-stop's call while another thread waits in wait_done or a deep arm/run is not shown. Upstream defect, not served: check_compatibility reads the toolkit attribute without calling it (base.py:86).
